tells: 1. The laugh doesn't land. Across 1.0 s only the woman in the white cardigan lifts a hand to her chest; every other face stays neutral and every head holds still, so nothing reads as a reaction to a line (club-5-strip.png, all six frames, front row)

2. The front rows are lit flat and frontal, like an on-camera flash. Candles burn on every table but no warm underlight reaches chins or hands, so the practicals don't motivate the key and faces look evenly lit, CG and plastic (club-1-wide.png and club-6-held.png, front two rows, centre)

3. Most of the room repeats the same resting pose: forearms on the table, hands clasped by the candle, torso square to the stage. It reads as a row of mannequins posed alike (club-6-held.png and club-1-wide.png, front tables, centre to right)

4. The back of the house is solid black cut-out silhouettes with no rim, no falloff and no depth gradation. They read as cardboard flats against the haze, not as people (club-1-wide.png, upper middle band behind row 2; club-2-mid.png, upper left)

5. On the face close, depth-of-field matting leaves a dark halo along the hair and shoulder, and the skin is waxy with glassy eyes and no specular life. The smile is a stiff half-mouth rather than an expression (club-4-face.png, left hair edge and right shoulder edge; face centre)

1. The front rows read as a police lineup. Several people sit square to camera, knees apart, hands on the knees, all upright. The posture is stiff and symmetric, and nobody slouches, leans or crosses a leg (theatre-1-wide.png, front two rows, centre)

2. Texture or shading dropouts: a background figure has a flat white rectangular torso, and the front-left woman's arms are untextured, uniform grey-white, so they look like a mannequin's (theatre-6-held.png, left edge mid-height and lower-left foreground)

3. In the back rows, faces are lit much brighter than the bodies and seats around them. Heads look like floating, pasted-on masks rather than people sitting in shadow (theatre-2-mid.png, upper left man around x150-220 y200-290; theatre-3-mid.png, mid-back row)

4. There is no laugh build across the strip. Frames t=12.0 to 12.6 are nearly identical, and only at t=12.8 to 13.0 do a couple of people turn their heads and one man gestures. Nobody laughs, so the reaction doesn't read as caused by a line (theatre-5-strip.png, all frames)

5. The edge of the light pool is hard and the rows behind fall to near-black cut-outs with a cool blue haze. The depth separation is good, but the silhouettes are flat and repeat the same head shapes, which betrays the impostors (theatre-1-wide.png, rows 3 and back, full width)

1. Posture: much of the front row sits with hands on the knees and shins vertical, and one woman's bare pink legs look clipped or mis-skinned against her shorts (openmic-1-wide.png, front row centre; legs at around x700-800 y600-700)

2. One face looks deformed: a back-row man has a beige blob or protrusion over his nose and mouth, and the red-jacket man's eye sockets are blotchy and dark (openmic-3-mid.png, centre top around x490-520 y320-370; right around x960-1010 y320-380)

3. The face close has visible artefacts: aliased, striped hair cards and a dark matte halo around the head and shoulder from depth-of-field compositing. The skin is smooth and porcelain-like (openmic-4-face.png, right side of the head and the collar edge)

4. Light motivation: the row of evenly spaced, identical downlights on a flat back wall looks like a game level. The front row is filled flat and evenly, the stage spill has no direction, and the left wall glows from an unexplained source (openmic-1-wide.png, upper band and left wall; openmic-6-held.png, upper left)

5. The reaction is social, not comic. From t=12.6 to 13.0 the two women turn to each other and smile, but the faces open only a little, and the man in the yellow henley and the man in the denim jacket barely change. It reads as chatting rather than a laugh building on a line (openmic-5-strip.png, centre and left)
